purpose: Esomeprazole is used to reduce the amount of acid your stomach makes. It helps treat conditions like heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), stomach ulcers, and damage to your esophagus caused by too much acid. It can also help prevent ulcers in people who take certain pain medications like ibuprofen regularly.
how_it_works: Your stomach has tiny pumps that produce acid to help digest food. Esomeprazole works by blocking these pumps so they make much less acid. With less acid, your stomach and esophagus have a chance to heal, and your symptoms like heartburn and pain get much better.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication well, but some may experience headache, nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, or constipation. Some people notice a dry mouth or feel a little gassy. These side effects are usually mild and tend to go away on their own.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you are allergic to esomeprazole or similar medications like omeprazole or pantoprazole. Taking it for a long time or at high doses may lower your magnesium and vitamin B12 levels, and may slightly increase your risk of bone fractures. Tell your doctor if you notice any muscle cramps, irregular heartbeat, or unusual fatigue. Also let your doctor know about all other medications you take, as this drug can interact with several common medicines.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the typical dose is 20 to 40 mg taken once a day, usually in the morning about 30 to 60 minutes before eating. Your doctor will decide the right dose and how long you should take it based on your condition. For over-the-counter heartburn use, adults typically take 20 mg once daily for 14 days.
